name: Grandmother's Field Journal
tagline: Gran's watercolor sketchbook on the Wolf, with every villager taped in.
motifs: Deckled cold-press pages lying open on dark green bookcloth, with a red ribbon
Villagers as taped-in polaroids over real watercolor washes
Hand-inked watercolor map of the path from the village
Pressed ferns, oak and birch leaves, forget-me-nots
Washi tape, photo corners and torn ruled notebook sheets
reveal: A madder-red watercolor bleed blooms over the Wolf's slip and its paw prints walk across it back to the Wolf's portrait as 'It was the Wolf!' inks in red, while a pressed forget-me-not rubber stamp thumps 'The real Maya' onto the true answer.
why: The open journal sits on a dark cloth surround, so the projector shows bright pages in a dim room without blasting white, and the code, prompt and answers are big, high-contrast type laid on top of the craft. Truth is green, the Wolf is red, so the whole room reads the reveal from across the floor before anyone reads a word.
